_provenance.derivation_policy: structure only. No mark-scheme or report wording is reproduced in learner-facing output.
_provenance.validation: Computed parts are counts over the evidence file. 'points listed' is read from the evidence records' own descriptions of each part's marking points (n=18 parts with a readable count); it is a count of ideas on the scheme, not a quote.

8223.subject: NSSCAS Biology 8223

P1.name: Theory: Multiple choice questions
P1.description: This paper consists of forty multiple-choice items of the four-choice type. The questions will be based on content described as specific objectives and will test abilities in assessment objectives A and B. Candidates will answer all questions. Candidates will answer on an answer sheet.

P2.name: Theory: Structured questions
P2.description: This paper will consist of compulsory short- answer, structured and free-response questionsa variable number of questions, of variable mark value.The questions will test skills and abilities in Assessment Objectives A and B. Learners will answer all questions on the question paper [booklet].

P3.name: Advanced Practical Skills
P3.description: This paper requires learners to carry out practical work in timed conditions. Learners will be expected to collect, record and analyse data so that they can answer questions related to the activity. The paper will consist of two experiments drawn from different areas of Biology. Learners will answer all questions. Learners will answer on the question paper. These questions may be based on the practical work in this syllabus with which the learner is familiar. They may also include practical exercises unfamiliar to the learner, but if this is the case then sufficient explanation and instruction will be given to enable the learner to use knowledge of practical work in other areas to complete the task satisfactorily. Centres are expected to have standard laboratory facilities available for all of their learners.

mark_scheme_conventions.meaning: Marking points are numbered; a later point can depend on an earlier one (a point is not credited unless the one it depends on is).
A different wording of the same idea earns the same credit.
The argument made the other way round earns the same credit.
Some answers are explicitly accepted, rejected or ignored (2025 uses A and R prefixes); a reject on a wrong word can cancel an otherwise right answer.
Marks from one group of points are capped (for example a maximum of 2 for the explanation, or 1 for only listing stages).
A wrong answer in one part is not penalised again where it feeds a later part that is otherwise correct.
Where a question asks for a number of items, only the first answers on the answer lines are marked.
A creditworthy point not on the scheme can earn a mark.

8223.mark_scheme_conventions_note: Years come from a count of these conventions inside each report's Biology section (page ranges not asserted except where a verified_page is given).

answer_style_rules_from_reports.rule: Answer describe, explain, suggest, discuss, give a reason and outline questions in full sentences; use bullet points only when asked to list or state.
Use the number of marks to decide how many steps or reasons to give.
Refer to the data given at least once, with the unit, to reach the top mark on a data question.
Terminology and spelling are credited: a misspelled or wrong term (for example 'PH' for pH) can lose the mark.
Answer the question set: describing a graph is not explaining it; naming a stage is not giving its reason.
